title: DRINKING WATER TREATMENT AND HEALTH RISK REDUCTION IN SMALL ISLAND COMMUNITIES: A BIBLIOMETRIC REVIEW

DRINKING WATER TREATMENT AND HEALTH RISK REDUCTION IN SMALL ISLAND COMMUNITIES: A BIBLIOMETRIC REVIEW

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Marwah Nur Fajrin, Agus Bintara Birawida, Nurul Syahriani Salahuddin, Yuanita Windusari, Anie Yulistyorini, Shaharuddin Mohd Sham, Muhammad Nasir,

ABSTRACT

This bibliometric review examines drinking water treatment technologies and contribution to environmental health risk reduction in small island communities. A scopus search identified 1,134 articles published between 2016 and April 2026. After removing duplicates and records with incomplete author information, 874 articles included in the bibliometric analysis, were analyzed using VOSviewer version 1.6.21 and Biblioshiny package version 5.4.1 in RStudio version 2026.07.0+139, while 30 articles from 18 countries were selected for evidence synthesis following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Water quality was a dominant research theme, while drinking water treatment and health risk reduction were weakly linked. Microbial contamination, particularly Escherichia coli and fecal coliforms, was frequently reported alongside salinity, fluoride, arsenic, heavy metals, and disinfection by-products. Technologies reviewed included rainwater harvesting, point-of-use interventions, electrocoagulation, electrodialysis, and reverse osmosis. However, no single technology can address all water quality challenges in small islands. Only 8 of the 30 articles (26.7%) directly linked water treatment performance to measurable reductions in health risks. Successful implementation technologies depend on local water conditions, maintenance, operational capacity, institutional responsibility, and system resilience.Further studies are needed to integrate water source conservation, contaminant specific clean water treatment, post-treatment risk assessment, and continuous monitoring simultaneously.
